item.title: MemGUI-Bench: Benchmarking Memory of Mobile GUI Agents in Dynamic Environments
item.description: Reliable mobile GUI agents must retain and reuse information across actions, applications, and repeated interactions. However, current benchmarks systematically underrepresent these memory demands: only 5.2-11.8 percent of their tasks are memory-related, and none evaluates cross-session learning. item.title: Quantitative control and recording of materials-synthesis processes using an automated experimentation platform
item.description: Data-driven materials development requires the collection of large amounts of high-quality materials data. Full autonomy of materials experiments is anticipated, but its technical hurdles are high and its adoption remains limited. item.title: Self-directed coaching: repositioning the client as the internalizing agent of developmental self-regulation a conceptual framework and research agenda for coaching theory and practice
item.description: Coaching has become one of the most widely deployed developmental interventions in organizational, educational, and health-professions settings, and the literature offers substantial evidence for its short-term benefits. Evidence on whether those benefits persist after formal coaching support is withdrawn is thinner and less systematic, and the question points to an unresolved tension at the field’s core. item.title: Agentic Software Engineering: Foundational Pillars and a Research Roadmap
item.description: Agentic Software Engineering (SE 3.0) represents a new era where intelligent agents are tasked not with simple code generation, but with achieving complex, goal-oriented SE objectives. item.title: Safe Recovery of AI Agents in Enterprise Systems: Preventing Duplicate Actions and Preserving Human Corrections
item.description: Reliable use of AI agents in enterprise systems depends on what happens after an action fails or its outcome becomes uncertain. Retrying can duplicate an order, while reversing a workflow can invalidate a person’s subsequent correction. The central challenge is deciding whether recovery is justified by the available evidence and still satisfies the business request. item.description: Abstract How should a language model be specialized for a target task when training is limited to one consumer GPU and a few hours? item.description: The rapid growth of Artificial Intelligence-generated content (AIGC) is reshaping video production and circulation, exposing children to an increasing volume of AIGC videos. item.description: Abstract The emergence of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) systems has fundamentally altered the epistemological conditions under which educational research is conducted, rendering existing faculty preparation frameworks necessary but insufficient. item.title: Self-evolving Embodied AI
item.description: Abstract Embodied Artificial Intelligence (AI) is an intelligent system formed by agents and their environment through active perception, embodied cognition, and action interaction. item.description: Abstract Background Deep learning-based systems have demonstrated high performance in automated Tuberculosis (TB) detection from chest X-ray (CXR) images and are increasingly considered for large-scale screening. item.description: Abstract Research Summary Entrepreneurs and managers often need to evaluate strategic choices, such as redesigning an incentive plan or entering an unfamiliar market, before committing scarce resources. item.description: Abstract The rapid adoption of generative artificial intelligence (GenAI) in higher education has created a significant assessment gap, as students increasingly submit AI-assisted work without demonstrating competencies required to verify facts, authenticate sources, identify hallucinations, assess bias, uphold academic integrity, and critically reflect on AI use. item.title: CUA-Master: Scaling Computer-use Agents through Open-World Recursive Improvements
item.description: Despite recent advances in CUAs, their development remains constrained by the limited diversity, controllability, and reliability of interaction data. item.description: When a masked diffusion language model is sampled in a few parallel steps in a random order, the model actually run is a mixture over reveal plans, while cross-entropy training fits token conditionals rather than this mixture.
